result.summary: Passes base32 I2P addresses directly to the SAM bridge `STREAM CONNECT` command rather than issuing a preliminary `NAMING LOOKUP` command. This eliminates a round trip to the local SAM bridge on every outbound I2P connection.
result.problem: Outbound I2P connections perform a redundant `NAMING LOOKUP` step that adds latency. Furthermore, when unresolvable peers cause the lookup to return an empty `VALUE=` key, Bitcoin Core treats it as an internal proxy error rather than a peer reachability failure, preventing AddrMan from recording the failed attempt.
evidence: PR description quotes the SAM v3 API specification stating that STREAM CONNECT accepts `.b32.i2p` as DESTINATION (https://i2p.net/en/docs/api/samv3/#sam-virtual-streams-connect)
PR description notes minimum router versions supporting this (Java I2P 0.9.48, i2pd 2.38.0) are older than encryption type requirements already merged in #35696
result.card: Passes base32 I2P addresses directly to the SAM `STREAM CONNECT` command, removing a redundant preliminary `NAMING LOOKUP` round trip on outbound I2P connections. When peer lookups fail under the old approach, empty responses are treated as local proxy errors rather than unreachable peers, preventing AddrMan from recording the failed connection attempt. The SAM v3 specification supports base32 destinations directly across all supported I2P router implementations.

risk.why: A flaw in the SAM command formatting or compatibility could break outbound I2P connections for node operators using I2P.
